title: RamosLabs DS vs Material Design vs Tailwind CSS: which should I use?
summary: RamosLabs DS ships tokens and documentation without components yet, while Material Design and Tailwind CSS differ in what they deliver.
short: Choose RamosLabs DS when you want a documented mono-indigo token set and patterns to build your own components on, with no component library required. Choose Material Design when you need a full component ecosystem, or Tailwind CSS when you want utility classes on a visual system you define; RamosLabs tokens can be consumed from Tailwind as CSS variables.

sections.heading: What each one is
body: RamosLabs DS is a mono-indigo, taxonomy-first design system. Its tokens (color, spacing, typography, radius, shadow, and motion) are defined once and compiled to CSS variables, TypeScript values, and a flat JSON map. The system also ships documentation covering foundations and patterns such as forms, tables, modals, and accessibility.
Material Design is Google's design system. It provides guidelines, Material 3 color roles, and a component ecosystem that teams can build on.

Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework. It ships with a default theme and lets you configure design tokens, so teams compose styles from utility classes instead of writing component stylesheets.

sections.heading: Where RamosLabs is not the right choice
body: RamosLabs DS does not ship a component library yet. The planned SJ components in @ramoslabs/vue are not released, so until then you build components from the tokens and the documented patterns. If you need ready-made components today, a component ecosystem such as Material Design fits that need better.
The tokens do not generate layouts or components. They supply values such as --space-6 and --radius-lg, and you still write the markup and styles that use them.
The system is built around one action accent, Indigo 600 (#4f46e5), with violet as a decorative accent only. A brand that needs several interactive colors would need a different palette.

sections.heading: When to choose each
body: Choose RamosLabs DS when you want a documented token set with a single action accent, you plan to build your own components, and you want agent tooling such as the MCP server and llms.txt files to read the system.
Choose Material Design when you want a component ecosystem that follows Google's guidelines and Material 3 color roles, and you accept that layout and component decisions follow that system.
Choose Tailwind CSS when you want utility classes for fast composition and you will define your own visual system in the theme configuration.

sections.heading: Using them together
body: The tools do not exclude each other. RamosLabs tokens are framework-agnostic CSS variables, so they work in a Tailwind project. Import the tokens once at the app entry, then reference the variables. Tailwind's default palette classes do not read RamosLabs tokens unless you map them in the theme, so reference the variables directly, for example with arbitrary properties.

sections.heading: Review note
body: The Material Design and Tailwind CSS descriptions in this page are summaries of their structure, written without version numbers, statistics, or quality claims. Verify them against the official Material Design and Tailwind CSS documentation before relying on them. The RamosLabs DS facts come from its published token values, package details, and documentation.

faq.q: Does RamosLabs DS include ready-made components?
faq.a: Not yet. The tokens and documentation are shipped, and a Vue component library with the SJ prefix in @ramoslabs/vue is planned but not released. Until then, build components from the tokens and the documented patterns.

faq.q: Can I use RamosLabs tokens with Tailwind CSS?
faq.a: Yes. Import the tokens CSS once at the app entry, then reference the CSS variables, for example with Tailwind arbitrary properties such as [background:var(--color-surface)].

faq.q: Is RamosLabs DS a replacement for Material Design?
faq.a: They address different needs. RamosLabs DS provides tokens and documented patterns to build on, while Material Design provides guidelines and a component ecosystem.

faq.q: Which tool fits a brand that uses one accent color?
faq.a: RamosLabs DS is built around one action accent, Indigo 600 (#4f46e5), with violet as a decorative accent only. If that model fits your brand, its tokens provide it directly.

faq.q: Does RamosLabs DS offer AI or agent tooling?
faq.a: Yes. It has a read-only MCP server at https://design.ramoslabs.com/mcp, llms.txt and llms-full.txt files, a registry.json, and an agent skill at /skill.md.

faq.q: Is RamosLabs DS free to use?
faq.a: Yes. The system is MIT licensed. Keep the copyright and license notice when you use it.
